messages:
maria: getting a 401 when streaming from our hosted API after rotating the API key in k8s secret. works in browser with old key but new key yields 401 in Rust client. anyone seen this?

josh: did you restart the pod / env reload? k8s secret update doesn't hot-swap into env of existing processes.

maria: yup — we rolled the Deployment, new pods have the new key. curl with the same header works from my laptop using the new key. only the Rust streaming client fails.

lee: quick checklist: 1) header format 2) trailing newline/CRLF 3) base64 padding 4) colon for empty password in basic auth 5) any proxy mangling headers

sanjay: fwiw we've bitten by pbcopy/paste adding a trailing \n on mac which changes base64 and causes a 401. try `echo -n` when encoding.

maria: ah — I copied from a secret editor and maybe included a newline. how should the auth header look exactly?

josh: Basic auth with api key-as-username and empty password -> header = `Authorization: Basic <base64(apiKey + ":")>`

lee: Rust example (reqwest):
```
let token = std::env::var("REDWOOD_API_KEY").expect("API key");
let auth = base64::encode(format!("{}:", token));
reqwest::Client::new()
    .get(url)
    .header("Authorization", format!("Basic {}", auth))
    .send()
    .await?;
```

maria: that's what we do, except we were using `base64::encode(token)` without the colon. :facepalm:

sanjay: also check CRLF vs LF — Windows/PowerShell might inject `\r`. You can quick-check length with `printf '%s' "$API_KEY" | wc -c` or `xxd -p` to spot trailing 0a/0d.

josh: Deno/TS snippet: `const auth = btoa(`${Deno.env.get("REDWOOD_API_KEY")}:`)` then `fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: 'Basic ' + auth } })`

maria: trying that now. also saw `systemd` + `EnvironmentFile=/etc/secret` once left a trailing newline when the file was written by our deploy script. worth checking systemd unit if anyone uses it.

lee: extra gotcha: k8s downwards API and projected secrets mounted as files include newline if secret value had one. `sed -n 'l' /path/to/secret` will show visible `\n`.

maria: fixed — I added the colon in the Rust encode and used `echo -n` when writing secrets. streaming now authenticates. thanks! :tada:

devx-bot: Deploybot: rotated `redwood-api-key` secret in namespace prod at 2026-03-16T14:02:00Z :white_check_mark:

josh: nice. follow-up: we should add a tiny integration test to SDKs that asserts header == computed value to catch this in CI. cc @maria @lee

maria: filing a quick PR after lunch.

lee: also adding a short note in docs about `Authorization: Basic <base64(apiKey:)>` and common ways to accidentally include newlines. :memo:
